result.target_summary: Nvidia's supply chain is concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region. New or existing export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations, negatively impacting the business.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose the impact of legislative changes, though on different specific regulatory topics. NVDA discusses risks related to export controls and supply chain concentration in the Asia-Pacific region, stating that 'new and existing export controls or changes to existing export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations and negatively impact our business.' Similarly, AMD discusses the impact of the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax legislation, noting that 'For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial,' while also continuing to evaluate further legislative changes. Both companies address the specific risk of regulatory/lawsuit impacts on their business operations and financials within Item 7.

sentences.text: While we work to enhance the resiliency and redundancy of our supply chain, which is currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, new and existing export controls or changes to existing export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations and negatively impact our business.
For 2024, the impact to us associated with Pillar Two was immaterial.
